issues.description: IdentityGrammar allows '+' sign on seed/increment which T-SQL does not accept
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar typically matches both '-' and '+'. T-SQL IDENTITY(seed, increment) accepts negative numbers but not a leading '+' sign. Using SignedSegmentGrammar without restricting to minus will parse IDENTITY(+1, +1) as valid, which SQL Server rejects. Consider matching only a minus sign here.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no documented justification
issues.detail: The PR description mentions only non-quoted identifier support for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, but the code also adds NumericLiteralSegment as a valid option. T-SQL's CREATE LOGIN DEFAULT_LANGUAGE expects a language name (identifier or string), not a numeric literal. No test covers this, and it appears to over-broaden the grammar.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE no longer accepts multiple comma-delimited actions in a single statement
issues.detail: The outer Delimited() wrapper was removed and replaced with OneOf(). The removed test case (ADD column_b ... , DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c) was valid T-SQL parsed previously. Removing this is a regression — mixed ADD/DROP within one ALTER TABLE is supported by SQL Server. The PR description frames this as 'invalid' but doesn't justify the claim.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT grammar makes CONSTRAINT keyword optional inside Delimited list
issues.detail: The inner Sequence wraps CONSTRAINT as optional, meaning 'ALTER TABLE t DROP SomeConstraint, SomeOtherConstraint' (without the CONSTRAINT keyword on either) could parse. The original outer-level grammar made CONSTRAINT optional only for legacy single-constraint syntax. Verify this doesn't accept invalid syntax silently.

issues.description: Test fixture for table variable with index has no trailing semicolon
issues.detail: The new declare_table_type.sql test case ends without a semicolon, unlike the prior cases in the file. This is parseable but inconsistent with the file's style and could mask issues with statement termination handling in batch parsing.

issues.description: No negative test for IDENTITY with negative increment
issues.detail: The new fixture exercises a negative seed IDENTITY(-2147483648, 1) but not a negative increment IDENTITY(1, -1), even though the grammar change adds SignedSegmentGrammar to both positions. Adding coverage would lock in the intended behavior.

review.summary: The PR extends TSQL parsing in four areas, mostly with reasonable test coverage. Main concerns: (1) IDENTITY now accepts a leading '+' sign which T-SQL does not permit; (2) DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts numeric literals which isn't justified by the PR description and isn't valid syntax; (3) the ALTER TABLE refactor removes the ability to combine multiple top-level actions (ADD column + DROP column) in one statement, which the PR labels invalid without citing docs — this looks like a regression. Minor nits around test consistency and missing negative-increment coverage.
